text: Alkaptonuria is an amino acid metabolism disorder. It is caused by mutations in the HGD gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Homogentisate 1,2-Dioxygenase. The metabolite that accumulates is Homogentisic Acid. Symptoms include arthritis and ochronosis. It is treated with nitisinone therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Arginase Deficiency is an amino acid metabolism disorder. It is caused by mutations in the ARG1 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Arginase 1. The metabolite that accumulates is Arginine. Symptoms include progressive intellectual disability and spasticity. It is treated with protein-restricted diet. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Argininosuccinic Aciduria is an amino acid metabolism disorder. It is caused by mutations in the ASL gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Argininosuccinate Lyase. The metabolite that accumulates is Argininosuccinic Acid. Symptoms include hyperammonemia and trichorrhexis nodosa. It is treated with arginine supplementation. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Ataxia-Telangiectasia is an other monogenic disorder. It is caused by mutations in the ATM gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is ATM Kinase. The metabolite that accumulates is Impaired DNA-Damage Response Marker. Symptoms include cerebellar ataxia and telangiectasia. It is treated with supportive care. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Beta-Ketothiolase Deficiency is an organic acidemia. It is caused by mutations in the ACAT1 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Beta-Ketothiolase. The metabolite that accumulates is 2-Methyl-3-Hydroxybutyric Acid. Symptoms include episodic ketoacidosis. It is treated with protein-restricted diet. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Biotinidase Deficiency is an other monogenic disorder. Biotinidase Deficiency is a cofactor-responsive disorder. It is caused by mutations in the BTD gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Biotinidase. The metabolite that accumulates is Biotin (Deficient). Symptoms include alopecia and seizures. It is treated with biotin supplementation. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Carnitine Palmitoyltransferase II Deficiency is a fatty acid oxidation disorder. It is caused by mutations in the CPT2 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Carnitine Palmitoyltransferase II. The metabolite that accumulates is Long-Chain Acylcarnitines. Symptoms include exercise-induced myalgia and rhabdomyolysis. It is treated with low-fat high-carbohydrate diet. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I Deficiency is an urea cycle disorder. It is caused by mutations in the CPS1 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I. The metabolite that accumulates is Ammonia. Symptoms include coma and hyperammonemia. It is treated with protein-restricted diet. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Citrullinemia Type I is an amino acid metabolism disorder. It is caused by mutations in the ASS1 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Argininosuccinate Synthase. The metabolite that accumulates is Citrulline. Symptoms include hyperammonemia and lethargy. It is treated with protein-restricted diet. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Cystic Fibrosis is an other monogenic disorder. It is caused by mutations in the CFTR gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator. The metabolite that accumulates is Chloride Ion Transport (Defective). Symptoms include chronic lung infection and pancreatic insufficiency. It is treated with cftr modulator therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Fabry Disease is a lysosomal storage disorder. It is caused by mutations in the GLA gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Alpha-Galactosidase A. The metabolite that accumulates is Globotriaosylceramide. Symptoms include angiokeratoma, neuropathic pain and renal failure. It is treated with enzyme replacement therapy. Inheritance is x-linked.

Familial Hypercholesterolemia is an other monogenic disorder. It is caused by mutations in the LDLR gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is LDL Receptor. The metabolite that accumulates is LDL Cholesterol. Symptoms include early coronary artery disease and xanthomas. It is treated with statin therapy. Inheritance is autosomal dominant.

Fucosidosis is a lysosomal storage disorder. It is caused by mutations in the FUCA1 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Alpha-L-Fucosidase. The metabolite that accumulates is Fucose-Containing Glycolipids. Symptoms include angiokeratoma and coarse facial features. It is treated with supportive care. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Gaucher Disease is a lysosomal storage disorder. It is caused by mutations in the GBA gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Beta-Glucocerebrosidase. The metabolite that accumulates is Glucocerebroside. Symptoms include bone crises and hepatosplenomegaly. It is treated with enzyme replacement therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Glutaric Acidemia Type I is an organic acidemia. It is caused by mutations in the GCDH gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Glutaryl-CoA Dehydrogenase. The metabolite that accumulates is Glutaric Acid. Symptoms include dystonic movement disorder and macrocephaly. It is treated with carnitine supplementation with lysine restriction. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Glycogen Storage Disease Type III (Cori Disease) is a glycogen storage disease. It is caused by mutations in the AGL gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Glycogen Debranching Enzyme. The metabolite that accumulates is Limit Dextrin. Symptoms include hepatomegaly and hypoglycemia. It is treated with high-protein diet. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Glycogen Storage Disease Type I (Von Gierke Disease) is a glycogen storage disease. It is caused by mutations in the G6PC gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Glucose-6-Phosphatase. The metabolite that accumulates is Glycogen. Symptoms include hepatomegaly and hypoglycemia. It is treated with uncooked cornstarch therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Glycogen Storage Disease Type V (McArdle Disease) is a glycogen storage disease. It is caused by mutations in the PYGM gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Myophosphorylase. The metabolite that accumulates is Glycogen. Symptoms include exercise intolerance and myalgia. It is treated with avoidance of strenuous exercise. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Hartnup Disease is an amino acid metabolism disorder. It is caused by mutations in the SLC6A19 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Neutral Amino Acid Transporter B(0)AT1. The metabolite that accumulates is Tryptophan. Symptoms include cerebellar ataxia and pellagra-like rash. It is treated with nicotinamide supplementation. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Hereditary Hemochromatosis is an other monogenic disorder. It is caused by mutations in the HFE gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is HFE Protein. The metabolite that accumulates is Iron. Symptoms include diabetes mellitus and liver cirrhosis. It is treated with therapeutic phlebotomy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Holocarboxylase Synthetase Deficiency is an other monogenic disorder. Holocarboxylase Synthetase Deficiency is a cofactor-responsive disorder. It is caused by mutations in the HLCS gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Holocarboxylase Synthetase. The metabolite that accumulates is Mixed Organic Acids. Symptoms include seizures and skin rash. It is treated with biotin supplementation. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Homocystinuria is an amino acid metabolism disorder. It is caused by mutations in the CBS gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Cystathionine Beta-Synthase. The metabolite that accumulates is Homocysteine. Symptoms include lens dislocation, marfanoid habitus and thromboembolism. It is treated with vitamin b6 supplementation. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Isovaleric Acidemia is an organic acidemia. It is caused by mutations in the IVD gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Isovaleryl-CoA Dehydrogenase. The metabolite that accumulates is Isovaleric Acid. Symptoms include sweaty feet odor and vomiting. It is treated with leucine-restricted diet with glycine. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Krabbe Disease is a lysosomal storage disorder. It is caused by mutations in the GALC gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Galactocerebrosidase. The metabolite that accumulates is Psychosine. Symptoms include demyelination and irritability. It is treated with hematopoietic stem cell transplant. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Long-Chain 3-Hydroxyacyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency is a fatty acid oxidation disorder. It is caused by mutations in the HADHA gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Long-Chain 3-Hydroxyacyl-CoA Dehydrogenase. The metabolite that accumulates is 3-Hydroxy Fatty Acids. Symptoms include peripheral neuropathy and retinopathy. It is treated with mct oil dietary therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome is an other monogenic disorder. It is caused by mutations in the HPRT1 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Hypoxanthine-Guanine Phosphoribosyltransferase. The metabolite that accumulates is Uric Acid. Symptoms include gout and self-injurious behavior. It is treated with allopurinol therapy. Inheritance is x-linked.

Medium-Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency is a fatty acid oxidation disorder. It is caused by mutations in the ACADM gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Medium-Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase. The metabolite that accumulates is Medium-Chain Fatty Acids. Symptoms include hypoketotic hypoglycemia and lethargy. It is treated with avoidance of fasting. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Malonic Aciduria is an organic acidemia. It is caused by mutations in the MLYCD gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Malonyl-CoA Decarboxylase. The metabolite that accumulates is Malonic Acid. Symptoms include cardiomyopathy and developmental delay. It is treated with low-fat diet. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Maple Syrup Urine Disease is an amino acid metabolism disorder. It is caused by mutations in the BCKDHA gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Branched-Chain Alpha-Ketoacid Dehydrogenase. The metabolite that accumulates is Leucine. Symptoms include encephalopathy and sweet-smelling urine. It is treated with branched-chain amino acid restricted diet. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Menkes Disease is an other monogenic disorder. It is caused by mutations in the ATP7A gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Copper-Transporting ATPase 1. The metabolite that accumulates is Copper (Deficient). Symptoms include hair abnormalities and progressive neurodegeneration. It is treated with copper histidine injections. Inheritance is x-linked.

Metachromatic Leukodystrophy is a lysosomal storage disorder. It is caused by mutations in the ARSA gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Arylsulfatase A. The metabolite that accumulates is Sulfatide. Symptoms include demyelination and gait disturbance. It is treated with hematopoietic stem cell transplant. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Methylmalonic Acidemia is an organic acidemia. Methylmalonic Acidemia is a cofactor-responsive disorder. It is caused by mutations in the MUT gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Methylmalonyl-CoA Mutase. The metabolite that accumulates is Methylmalonic Acid. Symptoms include failure to thrive and metabolic acidosis. It is treated with vitamin b12 supplementation. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I (Hurler Syndrome) is a lysosomal storage disorder. It is caused by mutations in the IDUA gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Alpha-L-Iduronidase. The metabolite that accumulates is Dermatan Sulfate. Symptoms include coarse facial features and hepatosplenomegaly. It is treated with enzyme replacement therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Mucopolysaccharidosis Type II (Hunter Syndrome) is a lysosomal storage disorder. It is caused by mutations in the IDS gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Iduronate-2-Sulfatase. The metabolite that accumulates is Heparan Sulfate. Symptoms include coarse facial features and joint stiffness. It is treated with enzyme replacement therapy. Inheritance is x-linked.

N-Acetylglutamate Synthase Deficiency is an urea cycle disorder. It is caused by mutations in the NAGS gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is N-Acetylglutamate Synthase. The metabolite that accumulates is Ammonia. Symptoms include hyperammonemia. It is treated with carglumic acid therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Niemann-Pick Disease Type A is a lysosomal storage disorder. It is caused by mutations in the SMPD1 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Acid Sphingomyelinase. The metabolite that accumulates is Sphingomyelin. Symptoms include hepatosplenomegaly and progressive neurodegeneration. It is treated with supportive care. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Nonketotic Hyperglycinemia is an amino acid metabolism disorder. It is caused by mutations in the GLDC gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Glycine Decarboxylase. The metabolite that accumulates is Glycine. Symptoms include encephalopathy and seizures. It is treated with sodium benzoate therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Ornithine Transcarbamylase Deficiency is an urea cycle disorder. It is caused by mutations in the OTC gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Ornithine Transcarbamylase. The metabolite that accumulates is Orotic Acid. Symptoms include hyperammonemia and vomiting. It is treated with protein-restricted diet. Inheritance is x-linked.

Phenylketonuria is an amino acid metabolism disorder. It is caused by mutations in the PAH gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Phenylalanine Hydroxylase. The metabolite that accumulates is Phenylalanine. Symptoms include intellectual disability and microcephaly. It is treated with low-phenylalanine diet. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Pompe Disease is a lysosomal storage disorder. It is caused by mutations in the GAA gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Acid Alpha-Glucosidase. The metabolite that accumulates is Glycogen. Symptoms include cardiomyopathy and muscle weakness. It is treated with enzyme replacement therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Primary Carnitine Deficiency is a fatty acid oxidation disorder. It is caused by mutations in the SLC22A5 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is OCTN2 Carnitine Transporter. The metabolite that accumulates is Free Carnitine (Deficient). Symptoms include cardiomyopathy and muscle weakness. It is treated with carnitine supplementation. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Propionic Acidemia is an organic acidemia. Propionic Acidemia is a cofactor-responsive disorder. It is caused by mutations in the PCCA gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Propionyl-CoA Carboxylase. The metabolite that accumulates is Propionic Acid. Symptoms include hyperammonemia and lethargy. It is treated with protein-restricted diet with biotin. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Refsum Disease is a peroxisomal disorder. It is caused by mutations in the PHYH gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Phytanoyl-CoA Hydroxylase. The metabolite that accumulates is Phytanic Acid. Symptoms include peripheral neuropathy and retinitis pigmentosa. It is treated with dietary phytanic acid restriction. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Tay-Sachs Disease is a lysosomal storage disorder. It is caused by mutations in the HEXA gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Hexosaminidase A. The metabolite that accumulates is GM2 Ganglioside. Symptoms include cherry-red spot and progressive neurodegeneration. It is treated with supportive care. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

3-Methylcrotonyl-CoA Carboxylase Deficiency is an organic acidemia. It is caused by mutations in the MCCC1 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is 3-Methylcrotonyl-CoA Carboxylase. The metabolite that accumulates is 3-Methylcrotonylglycine. Symptoms include mild hypotonia. It is treated with carnitine supplementation. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Tyrosinemia Type I is an amino acid metabolism disorder. It is caused by mutations in the FAH gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Fumarylacetoacetase. The metabolite that accumulates is Succinylacetone. Symptoms include liver failure and renal tubular dysfunction. It is treated with nitisinone therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Very Long-Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency is a fatty acid oxidation disorder. It is caused by mutations in the ACADVL gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Very Long-Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase. The metabolite that accumulates is Long-Chain Fatty Acids. Symptoms include cardiomyopathy and hypoglycemia. It is treated with mct oil dietary therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

Wilson Disease is an other monogenic disorder. It is caused by mutations in the ATP7B gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Copper-Transporting ATPase 2. The metabolite that accumulates is Copper. Symptoms include hepatolenticular degeneration and kayser-fleischer rings. It is treated with penicillamine therapy. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.

X-Linked Adrenoleukodystrophy is a peroxisomal disorder. It is caused by mutations in the ABCD1 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is ALD Protein. The metabolite that accumulates is Very Long-Chain Fatty Acids. Symptoms include adrenal insufficiency and demyelination. It is treated with hematopoietic stem cell transplant. Inheritance is x-linked.

Zellweger Syndrome is a peroxisomal disorder. It is caused by mutations in the PEX1 gene. The deficient enzyme or protein is Peroxin-1. The metabolite that accumulates is Very Long-Chain Fatty Acids. Symptoms include craniofacial abnormalities and hypotonia. It is treated with supportive care. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.
